rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Furton Research Investment Committee assigns Alphabet Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.867. The dominant argument carrying the majority is that Alphabet represents a durable infrastructure business — anchored by Google's ~90% search share, YouTube's 2.7 billion monthly users, and Android's ecosystem — trading at a materially compressed forward multiple of approximately 14–15x earnings, offering an attractive entry point for a franchise of this quality and scale, now on a half-trillion-dollar revenue run rate with thirteen consecutive quarters of double-digit growth. The most significant dissent, advanced by Mr. Greenblatt, argued that unprecedented and opaque AI-related capital expenditures render forward returns on capital genuinely uncalculable, warranting a PASS. This view did not prevail because the majority concluded that AI infrastructure spending remains in its buildout phase rather than a disruption phase, and that Alphabet's competitive moats provide sufficient margin of safety at current valuations. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position in GOOGL at prevailing prices.

rows.name: American Express Co.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Furton Research Investment Committee assigns American Express a BUY rating with a composite score of 0.846. The dominant argument carrying the majority is that American Express's closed-loop network constitutes a durable, two-sided moat—affluent cardholders attract merchants, merchants attract cardholders—producing high returns on capital and a self-reinforcing competitive position that is exceptionally difficult to replicate. This thesis was endorsed with high conviction across three of four committee members. The most significant dissent, a PASS at low conviction, argued that American Express is defending an existing financial architecture rather than building a new one, and that disruptive digital and agentic commerce platforms may erode the franchise over time. This view did not prevail because the committee judged it inconsistent on its own terms: the dissenter acknowledged the closed-loop network as foundational to next-generation digital infrastructure yet declined to own it. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position in AXP at the verified price of $315.

rows.name: Walt Disney Co.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns a BUY rating to The Walt Disney Company with a conviction score of 0.84. The dominant argument carrying the majority is that Disney possesses one of the most durable consumer franchises in existence — built on multigenerational intellectual property, a $36 billion Experiences segment, and an improving streaming profitability trajectory — all available at a valuation well below prior peaks, creating a compelling pocket of relative value against the broader market. The most significant dissent, advanced by the disruptive-innovation perspective, argued that Disney is a legacy conglomerate defending existing entertainment real estate rather than creating new platform territory, and therefore unworthy of capital relative to higher-growth alternatives. This view did not prevail because the Committee concluded it conflated the question of growth rate with the question of risk-adjusted return, underweighting the franchise's pricing power, asset irreplaceability, and attractive earnings yield at current levels. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position in DIS at prevailing prices.

rows.name: Amazon.com Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) a BUY rating with a composite score of 0.733. The dominant argument, advanced by a majority comprising Aschenbrenner, Marks, and Wood, holds that AWS constitutes a durable AI infrastructure franchise — evidenced by 38.7% operating margins, a $578 billion backlog, and sevenfold Bedrock growth among the Fortune 500 — trading at a historically compressed 22x forward earnings that represents a genuine second-level thinking opportunity rather than fair pricing. The most significant dissent, articulated by Buffett and Greenblatt, contended that relentless capital reinvestment obscures true return on capital and that the earnings power implied by current valuations depends on uncertain AI capex returns through 2030. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the capital intensity to be precisely the competitive moat under construction, not a deficiency in the thesis, and found the valuation anomaly sufficiently compelling relative to the quality and scale of the franchise. The Committee recommends establishing a BUY position at current levels.

rows.name: Salesforce Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Salesforce Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.704. The dominant argument carrying the majority rests on the durability of Salesforce's competitive moat — thirteen consecutive years of CRM market leadership, switching costs deeply embedded across enterprise workflows, and a valuation compressed to approximately 17x trailing earnings following an 18% year-over-year share price decline, offering an attractive entry point for a franchise of this caliber. Margin expansion and early Agentforce monetization further support the thesis. The most significant dissent, advanced by Aschenbrenner and Greenblatt, centered on the risk that agentic AI could commoditize Salesforce's core platform through the 2027–2028 window, compounded by concerns over inflated goodwill obscuring true returns on capital. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the disruption risk to be longer-dated and substantially reflected in the current depressed multiple. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels with ongoing monitoring of Agentforce adoption trajectory and competitive AI developments.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns NVIDIA a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.69. The dominant argument that carried the majority was the recognition, advanced most forcefully by Ms. Wood and ultimately endorsed by Mr. Buffett and Mr. Aschenbrenner, that a 21.8x price-to-earnings multiple on a business compounding revenue at 103% year-over-year with 74.8% gross margins and 66.9% operating margins represents genuine value on a growth-adjusted basis — not the speculative excess several members initially assumed. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Marks, who cautioned that extraordinary business quality does not guarantee investment merit when enthusiasm may already be embedded in the price, and from Mr. Greenblatt, who questioned the sustainability of normalized earnings. These objections did not prevail because the current valuation, grounded in actual earnings rather than projected multiples, already discounts meaningful reversion risk. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels with disciplined sizing appropriate to the CEO-transition uncertainty and geopolitical exposure noted in the record.

rows.name: Travelers Cos. Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns The Travelers Companies, Inc. (TRV) a final score of **0.684** and recommends a **BUY** position. The dominant argument, advanced by Mr. Buffett and ultimately endorsed by a majority including Mr. Greenblatt, rested on Travelers' exceptional underwriting discipline — a combined ratio of 86.8% sustained over nine consecutive profitable quarters — paired with intelligent float deployment and a trailing P/E of 9.55, which together present a compelling value proposition for steady capital compounding. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Marks, who argued that a 40% single-year price surge and broad analyst upgrades have already priced in this underwriting excellence, leaving insufficient margin of safety at current levels. His objection did not prevail because the majority judged that the durability of Travelers' sub-87% combined ratio and 22% core ROE represent structural earning power not yet fully reflected in the valuation. The Committee recommends initiating a position in TRV at current prices, with ongoing monitoring of catastrophe-loss trends and reserve adequacy.

rows.name: Nike Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee adopts a BUY position on Nike Inc. with a conviction score of 0.667. The dominant argument, advanced by Marks and Greenblatt and carrying the majority, holds that Nike's current valuation — 17.9x trailing earnings against a five-year median of approximately 30x, and just 1.2x revenue — already discounts the severity of the company's operational headwinds, presenting a compelling mean-reversion opportunity in a franchise possessing durable economic goodwill and genuine pricing power. The most significant dissent came from Buffett, who cautioned that the forward P/E of nearly 30x implies the market is already pricing in a substantial earnings recovery that may not materialize, and that franchise erosion risk warrants greater conservatism. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the trailing-multiple compression to be sufficiently extreme to provide an adequate margin of safety even under delayed-recovery scenarios. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels with disciplined sizing appropriate to the uncertainty surrounding the pace of brand recovery.

rows.name: Caterpillar Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has reached a final position of **BUY** on Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) with a conviction score of **0.632**. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and Joel Greenblatt, held that the approximately 44–46% drawdown from the June high has materially repriced a world-class industrial franchise, creating an attractive margin of safety even at a trailing 22x P/E—particularly given the structural growth opportunity in Energy & Transportation, where data-center generator demand introduces a durable, less cyclical earnings stream. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett, who argued that a cyclical industrial trading at 22x trailing earnings remains priced like a compounder and lacks the recession-resistant characteristics he demands for deployment of capital. This objection did not prevail because the majority judged that the magnitude of the drawdown, combined with the evolving business mix, sufficiently compensates for cyclical risk at current levels. The Committee recommends initiating a position in CAT at prevailing prices, with discipline around further entry should the price approach the bear-case range.

rows.name: Honeywell International Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns Honeywell Technologies (HON) a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.632. The dominant argument, advanced by Messrs. Greenblatt and Marks and carrying the majority, holds that the aerospace spin-off has created a classic orphan-stock dislocation: institutional holders are shedding shares indiscriminately, leaving a focused, high-return-on-capital automation business with genuine switching costs, 7% organic growth, a $19 billion backlog, and meaningful margin expansion trading below fair value during the transition period. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Buffett, who cautioned that the stark divergence between the trailing P/E of 9.39 and the forward P/E of 26.64 signals spin-off accounting distortion rather than a genuine bargain, and who questioned the long-term durability of Honeywell's competitive position against automation commoditization. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the trailing earnings figure to be temporarily depressed by one-time separation charges, not reflective of normalized earning power. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position, with particular attention to post-separation earnings normalization over the next two quarters.

rows.name: Microsoft Corp.
rows.statement: After full deliberation, the Investment Committee assigns Microsoft a final score of **0.5** and recommends a **BUY** position. The dominant argument that carried the majority holds that Microsoft occupies a singular position at the center of enterprise AI adoption, with Azure serving as the exclusive infrastructure host for OpenAI, Copilot monetizing across a 300-million-plus Office subscriber base, and AI revenue growing at 123% year-over-year — dynamics that make trailing valuation multiples inadequate for capturing the company's forward earnings trajectory. The most significant dissent, advanced consistently by three members, argued that at $3.76 trillion and 28x trailing earnings, Microsoft's extraordinary quality is already fully reflected in the price, and that conviction in AI adoption curves does not constitute the margin of safety prudent investment demands. This dissent did not prevail because the committee judged the structural depth of Microsoft's moat and its platform convergence positioning to be sufficiently differentiated to justify a modest premium entry. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position, sized to reflect the narrow margin of conviction.

rows.name: McDonald's Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns McDonald's a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.375. The dominant argument, advanced by Mr. Buffett and carrying the majority, holds that McDonald's operates not as a conventional restaurant business but as a royalty-stream franchise commanding extraordinary consumer-franchise economics—high aided brand awareness, 220 million loyalty program users, and durable pricing power rooted in the value of the product to the purchaser rather than its production cost. The most significant dissent, articulated by Messrs. Marks and Greenblatt, centered on valuation: at approximately 14x trailing earnings and 9.1x EV/Revenue, with U.S. comparable sales declining, the quality of the franchise may already be fully reflected in the current price. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged that the enduring franchise characteristics, global unit expansion trajectory toward 50,000 restaurants, and royalty-like capital-light cash flows justify a modest premium over near-term valuation metrics. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels with disciplined sizing appropriate to the moderate conviction score.

rows.name: Home Depot Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Home Depot a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.333. The dominant argument, advanced by Mr. Buffett and ultimately carrying the majority, held that Home Depot's 52% market share—sustained over two decades—its deepening Pro contractor relationships, and its unmatched distribution infrastructure constitute a durable competitive moat whose long-term compounding power justifies the current valuation of approximately 24× trailing earnings. The most significant dissent, articulated by Mr. Marks and Mr. Greenblatt, centered on the contention that the business's quality is already fully reflected in the price, with elevated multiples leaving insufficient margin of safety amid a soft housing cycle and tightened credit conditions. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged that the franchise's pricing power and structural dominance reduce the probability of permanent capital impairment sufficiently to warrant ownership at current levels. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position in HD, with sizing reflecting the narrow margin of safety acknowledged by all participants.
